AI Literacy Level 1: Build Book

One card per screen, in build order. Each card shows what the screen should look like, the exact text and voiceover, and the quickest way to build it in Storyline. Tick a screen off when it's done; ticks are saved in this browser only.

0 of 68 built

Routines used on every screen

Routine V
Voice. Insert > Audio > Text-to-Speech, paste the voiceover shown on the card, Language English (India), the same Neural voice every time, tick Create closed captions, Insert.
Routine T
Timing. Play the timeline and press C where each item should appear. Right-click each object in the Timeline > Align to Cue Point. Animations > Entrance > Fade, 0.5 s. Drag every bar to the end of the timeline.
Routine N
Next lock. Copy the two triggers from screen 2 (Disabled when the timeline starts; Normal when the timeline ends) and paste them. Set When revisiting: Resume saved state.
Quickest start
When a card says "Duplicate screen N", always do that rather than building from scratch: the layout, styles, triggers and timing come with the copy.

On-screen text

Level 1
Understand AI. Use It Responsibly.

Welcome to AI Literacy, Level 1. This course gives you a practical foundation for understanding AI, using it responsibly, and knowing where human judgment must remain at the center.

What You Will Learn

Build it

By the end of this course, you will be able to:
• Use AI effectively and understand its limitations

• Use basic prompting techniques to guide AI outputs

By the end of this course, you will be able to use AI effectively while understanding its limitations, use AI responsibly while protecting sensitive information, use basic prompting techniques to guide AI outputs, and describe what an AI agent is and why its work still needs human review.

W  Weigh the Output
A  Assess the Risk

What is AI?
How does generative AI work at a high level?
What language will you hear when people talk about AI?

Meera layer

Meera's manager says, "Just ask the AI. It knows everything." Meera has used a chatbot twice and isn't sure what "the AI" actually is.

What would you want to understand first?
1. What AI actually is, and what it does
   Reply: A strong place to start. Knowing what a tool is helps you judge what to expect from it.
2. Which buttons to press

3. Nothing. If it knows everything, just use it
   Reply: Hold that thought. By the end of this course you will see why "knows everything" is not quite true.

Let us begin with the foundation: what AI is, what generative AI means, and a few terms you need to recognize.

What Is Artificial Intelligence?

Build it

  1. Home > New Slide > Basic Layouts, pick Content S1, click Insert.
  2. Title: click the title area and type What Is Artificial Intelligence? (Aptos Display, bold, 44 pt, Pro Navy on light slides).
  3. AWARE badge: paste the badge group (from screen 6), set the letter to A and the word to Appreciate AI.
  4. Four capability cards, 466 × 150 each, two rows: fill E8EEFB, outline Pro Blue 497EDC 2 pt dashed, text Aptos 22 pt semibold navy: Recognize patterns · Interpret information · Generate content · Make predictions. Left cards left-aligned, right cards right-aligned.
  5. Centre card on top (350 × 170, navy fill, rounded): small label "AI" (Aptos Mono bold, Pro Teal) and the definition AI is technology that enables systems to perform tasks that typically require some form of human intelligence. (Aptos 21 pt, white, centred).
  6. The definition shows first; each card fades on its cue. Finish with Routines V, T and N (voice, timing, Next lock).

On-screen text

AI is technology that enables systems to perform tasks that typically require some form of human intelligence.

Recognize patterns  •  Interpret information  •  Generate content  •  Make predictions

Voiceover

Artificial intelligence is technology that enables systems to perform tasks that typically require some form of human intelligence. Depending on the technology, AI can recognize patterns, interpret information, generate content, and make predictions.

AI is not one single tool.

One important point is that AI is a broad field, not one single tool. Different AI systems can be designed for different capabilities. This course focuses on the concepts that apply across AI tools.

Generative AI creates new content from instructions and context.

TEXT   IMAGES   AUDIO   VIDEO   CODE

What Is a Large Language Model?

Build it

  1. Home > New Slide > Basic Layouts, pick Content S1, click Insert.
  2. Title: click the title area and type What Is a Large Language Model? (Aptos Display, bold, 44 pt, Pro Navy on light slides).
  3. Text A large language model (LLM) learns patterns from large amounts of data and uses those patterns to generate language. (Aptos 24 pt).
  4. Three boxes 330 × 150 in a row: "Data" (white card with a small grid of blue dots or a grid icon), "Language model" (navy fill, white text), "Response" (dashed Pro Blue outline, light blue fill, three grey bars for text lines).
  5. Two arrows between them (Insert > Shape > Right Arrow or a line with an arrowhead), Pro Blue. Don't add any tick or "verified" mark on the response.
  6. Data, arrow, model, arrow, response fade in order. Finish with Routines V, T and N (voice, timing, Next lock).

On-screen text

A large language model (LLM) learns patterns from large amounts of data and uses those patterns to generate language.

Voiceover

A large language model, or LLM, learns patterns from large amounts of data and uses those patterns to generate language in response to an instruction. It does this by predicting likely language from what it learned in training, which is why fluent output can still be wrong. The important point for Level 1 is that an LLM generates a response based on learned patterns. That does not mean the response has automatically been checked for accuracy.

Two Terms You Will Use Often

Build it

  2. Title: click the title area and type Two Terms You Will Use Often (Aptos Display, bold, 44 pt, Pro Navy on light slides).

On-screen text

PROMPT
The instruction you give AI

CONTEXT
Information that helps AI interpret the task

Voiceover

A prompt is the instruction you give an AI system. Context is the information that helps the system interpret what you need. You will use both ideas again when we cover prompting.

Three Terms to Recognize

Build it

On-screen text

HALLUCINATION
An inaccurate or unsupported AI output

BIAS
A pattern that can lead to unfair or distorted outcomes

AGENT
An AI system configured to carry out a defined task across multiple steps

Voiceover

A hallucination is an inaccurate or unsupported AI output. Bias can lead to unfair or distorted outcomes. An AI agent is a system configured to carry out a defined task across multiple steps using instructions, context, and available capabilities.

On-screen text

AI can support many kinds of work.
But capability does not equal reliability.

Meera layer

Meera asks AI to summarize 40 pages of survey comments. The summary is polished, and it includes a statistic she has not seen before.

What should Meera do with the summary?
1. Send it to leadership now
   Reply: Risky. A polished summary can still contain an error. This section shows why.
2. Check the statistic before using it
   Reply: Good call. Being useful and being reliable are two different things.
3. Ask the AI if it is sure
   Reply: AI can sound certain and still be wrong. You will see why in this section.

Meera voiceover: Meera has an AI-generated summary of forty pages of survey comments. It looks polished, and it includes a statistic she has not seen before. What should she do?

Voiceover

Now that you know what AI is, let us look at a critical distinction: what AI can do is not the same as what AI can reliably do.

One of the most important habits in working with AI is to separate confidence from correctness. An AI response can sound polished and certain while still containing an error.
Screen 19 · Storyboard slide 20 + 21 · Layout Question

Knowledge Check

Build it

  1. In Story View, right-click screen 12 > Duplicate, then drag the copy into place. Everything below is a change to that copy.
  2. Form View: question An AI tool gives you a confident answer containing a fact you cannot confirm. What should you do?; options A. Assume confidence means accuracy B. Use it immediately C. Verify the information using an appropriate reliable source D. Ask AI to sound more certain; tick C as correct.
  3. Feedback: Correct = AI can produce convincing but inaccurate information. Important facts should be verified.. Try Again and Incorrect = AI can sound confident even when it is wrong. Important information should be checked before use.. Incorrect layer also gets: The answer is C: Verify the information using an appropriate reliable source.

On-screen text

An AI tool gives you a confident answer containing a fact you cannot confirm.

What should you do?

A  Assume confidence means accuracy
B  Use it immediately
C  Verify the information using an appropriate reliable source
D  Ask AI to sound more certain

Feedback

Correct: AI can produce convincing but inaccurate information. Important facts should be verified.

Incorrect: AI can sound confident even when it is wrong. Important information should be checked before use.

Answer key: C

Select the response that best addresses an AI-generated answer that you cannot confirm.

On-screen text

Do not delegate sensitive decisions or accountability to AI.

Especially when decisions affect people or carry significant consequences.

AI can assist. Humans remain accountable.

Voiceover

There are situations where AI should support the process rather than make the decision. Do not delegate sensitive decisions or accountability to AI, especially when people may be affected or consequences are significant. In many places, decisions about employees and candidates are also covered by laws and policies that require human oversight. This is the core principle of the course: AI can assist, but humans remain accountable for how outputs are reviewed, used, and acted upon. Where your organization expects it, be open about when AI was used.

   Reply: Sometimes that's fine. But a few extra details can make AI much more useful.

Meera voiceover: Meera typed "Write an email" and got something generic that she can't use. What should she try next?

Voiceover

Once you know how AI works at a high level and how to use it responsibly, the next step is giving clear instructions. Prompting is simply communicating what you need from the system.

On-screen text

An AI agent is an AI system configured to carry out a defined task across multiple steps using:

INSTRUCTIONS  +  CONTEXT  +  AVAILABLE CAPABILITIES

Voiceover

At a high level, an AI agent is an AI system configured to carry out a defined task across multiple steps using instructions, context, and available capabilities. An agent can work through a defined task or sequence rather than simply returning one response. It can use tools to take actions, which is why its work still needs review.
Screen 51 · Storyboard slide 57 · Layout Content S7

Chatbot versus AI Agent

Build it

  1. Home > New Slide > Basic Layouts, pick Content S7, click Insert.
  2. Title: click the title area and type Chatbot versus AI Agent (Aptos Display, bold, 44 pt, Pro Navy on light slides).
  3. Two white rows. Row 1 "CHATBOT": pills "You ask" → "AI responds" and caption You ask → AI responds. Row 2 "AGENT": pills "You define a task" → "Step 1" → "Step 2" → "Step 3" and caption You define a task → Agent works through it.
  4. Pills: rounded, dashed Pro Blue; result pills filled Pro Blue with white text.
  5. Chatbot pills fade together; agent pills fade one by one. Finish with Routines V, T and N (voice, timing, Next lock).

On-screen text

CHATBOT
You ask → AI responds

AGENT
You define a task → Agent works through it

Voiceover

A chatbot typically responds to the request you make. An agent can be configured around a defined task and work through that task using its instructions, context, and capabilities. The difference is not the interface. An agent is set up to work through several steps toward a goal, often using tools, while a chatbot usually answers one request at a time.

On-screen text

An AI response is polished and persuasive but contains a claim you cannot verify. What should you do?

A  Use it because it sounds professional
B  Verify the claim before using it
C  Ask AI to make it more persuasive
D  Remove the source and keep the claim

Feedback

Correct: Correct. A polished answer is not necessarily accurate. Verify claims you cannot confirm before using them.

Incorrect: Not quite. Confidence and polish do not mean correctness. Verify the claim before using it.

Answer key: B
